items.headline: Garrett Wilson (concussion) injury update
items.news: Wilson (concussion) caught seven of 14 targets for 106 yards and lost a fumble in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.
items.analysis: Wilson set a new season high in targets and came one yard short of his Week 3 season high Sunday in his return from a one-game absence due to a concussion. His production came on a mix of passes from Geno Smith (ankle) and rookie Cade Klubnik, the latter of whom saw his first NFL action after Smith exited in the second half. Wilson figures to work as the top target for whomever starts under center in a Week 11 road game against the Chargers.

items.headline: Baker Mayfield (thumb) listed as questionable
items.news: Mayfield (thumb) is dealing with a plantar fascia injury in his foot, and he would wear a special orthotic and new cleats to stabilize his foot if he's cleared to play against the Lions on Sunday, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
items.analysis: Mayfield missed three games earlier in the season due to a dislocated right thumb, and he injured his foot during the Buccaneers' Week 9 loss to the Bears. He was in a walking boot during Tampa Bay's bye and received treatment on his foot during Week 11 prep, although head coach Todd Bowles told reporters Friday that Mayfield is "trending in the right direction" to play against Detroit. As it stands, Mayfield will be under center for the Buccaneers on Sunday, with undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels serving as the backup and Easton Stick operating as the emergency third quarterback.

items.headline: Geno Smith (ankle) injury update
items.news: Smith (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Chargers.
items.analysis: Smith dealt with an ankle injury during the week after he was forced from last Sunday's loss against the Bills, but all scans came back clean, and the veteran quarterback is good to go for a road date in Los Angeles. Smith has been able to get the ball to his playmakers this season, but he doesn't have any fantasy upside as a statuesque pocket passer in an offense that likes to run the ball.

items.headline: Kyle Monangai (toe) injury update
items.news: Monangai (toe) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game against the Saints.
items.analysis: After being listed as full on all three of the Bears' Week 11 practice reports, Monangai officially is in the clear for his first game action since Week 4, when he initially suffered a right thumb issue and a turf toe injury. While working in tandem with fellow RB D'Andre Swift this season, Monangai has racked up 60 carries for 324 yards and three touchdowns and caught all five targets for 39 yards in four appearances.

items.headline: Sione Vaki (ankle) listed as questionable
items.news: Vaki (ankle) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers.
items.analysis: If Vaki is unable to play against Tampa Bay, Jacob Saylors would move up to RB2 status, but Jahmyr Gibbs would have a chance to see an even bigger share of the backfield opportunities in that scenario.

items.headline: Roman Wilson (finger) nearing return from IR
items.news: Wilson (finger) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports.
items.analysis: Both Wilson and Michael Pittman (foot) are listed as questionable but remain on injured reserve. The duo could be activated Saturday if cleared to play against Philly. Wilson has been sidelined since injuring his finger in Week 5 against the Colts.

items.headline: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) remains on IR
items.news: Pittman (foot) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Mark Kaboly reports.
items.analysis: Pittman was designated for return from injured reserve earlier this week and had progressed to full participation Thursday, so his questionable tag keeps him in the mix for a potential activation ahead of Sunday's contest against the Eagles. With both Pittman and Roman Wilson (finger) nearing a return, it's unclear what that will mean for rookie Germie Bernard's role going forward, as the rookie has hit a slow spot in the box score the last couple weeks.

items.headline: Puka Nacua (knee) remains on IR
items.news: Coach Sean McVay revealed Friday that Nacua (knee) had surgery to repair his MCL on Tuesday and is on track to miss a couple of months, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
items.analysis: Given that timetable, Nacua -- who already is on injured reserve -- could be out for the rest of the regular season, which is a huge blow to the Rams' pass-catching corps going forward. In Nacua's continued absence, Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels, Tutu Atwell and Xavier Smith are the team's healthy options at WR, though fellow starter Davante Adams (hamstring) is believed to be targeting a return in Week 12 following the team's bye.

items.headline: Chris Bell (knee) injury update
items.news: Bell (knee) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Bills.
items.analysis: The rookie wideout is averaging 1.5 catches for 18.5 yards per game this season and is not in the conversation to start for fantasy teams with both Caleb Douglas and Malik Washington healthy.

items.headline: Caleb Douglas (shoulder) injury update
items.news: Douglas (shoulder) will play Sunday against the Bills, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
items.analysis: Douglas was managed during the practice week, but he's good to go for his normal every-down role Sunday against Buffalo. With the Dolphins installed as 16.5-point underdogs, Miami is projected to throw a ton in comeback mode. However, Douglas is a tough click for fantasy with Kyle McCord under center.

items.headline: Mike Evans (achilles) listed as questionable
items.news: Head coach Kyle Shanahan said Friday that the 49ers will make a decision on Evans' (Achilles) Week 11 status Saturday after listing the wide receiver as questionable for Sunday's game against the Vikings in Mexico City, Matt Barrows of ESPN.com reports.
items.analysis: Evans got back on the practice field Thursday as a limited participant, marking his first on-field work since aggravating his right Achilles during a Week 6 win versus the Commanders. Shanahan indicated that the team wants to see how Evans reacts to this week's practices before making a call on his availability for Sunday's showdown. In the end, though, San Francisco may not make an official ruling on Evans' status until about 90 minutes before an 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff.

items.headline: Chig Okonkwo (back) injury update
items.news: Okonkwo (back) returned to Thursday's eventual 24-21 win at the Giants, finishing with four catches (on eight targets) for 24 yards.
items.analysis: Okonkwo exited in the second quarter due to a back injury, but he was back out there on the field after halftime and was the target on both of Jayden Daniels' two interceptions with less than six minutes remaining in the contest. Overall, Okonkwo's eight targets marked a season high, but he also mustered his fewest receiving yards since Week 4. He'll look to build upon his season-long line of 27-263-0 on 39 targets in the Commanders' next game Monday, Nov. 23 versus the Bengals.

items.headline: Matt Gay (hip) listed as questionable
items.news: Gay (hip) was spotted at practice Friday, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
items.analysis: Gay, who was limited Wednesday, logged a DNP on Thursday, but it looks like he'll work in some capacity to close out the week. Per Warren, the Raiders worked out three kickers with Gay injured, but it appears as though it's only Gay and practice-squad member Kansei Matsuzawa available to handle kicks at Friday's practice.

items.headline: Jonathon Brooks (groin) remains on IR
items.news: Brooks (groin) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Ravens, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
items.analysis: Brooks remains on injured reserve, so the questionable tag suggests Carolina at least may activate him ahead of Sunday's contest. If he's cleared to play, the running back would be in line to make his first appearance since Week 2, though he's no real threat to Chuba Hubbard's standing as the Panthers' lead back.

items.headline: Kyler Murray (hamstring) ruled out
items.news: Murray (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday night's game against the 49ers.
items.analysis: The quarterback lost his job to Kirk Cousins and will continue to manage a hamstring injury. Murray's availability will only matter moving forward if something happens to Cousins, either performance or injury related. Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer remain on the 53-man roster as backup options.

items.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) listed as questionable
items.news: Burks (foot) did not practice Friday.
items.analysis: The Commanders have been managing Burks' practice reps, as he deals with a foot injury that's been nagging him for several weeks. He missed practice time last week but still was able to play against the Giants last Thursday, securing two of three targets for 27 yards. Washington will provide final injury designations Saturday ahead of Monday night's game against the Bengals.

items.headline: Rachaad White (heel) listed as questionable
items.news: White was limited at Friday's practice due to a heel injury.
items.analysis: White was tacked on to the Commanders' Week 11 practice report Friday, joining Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin), who has been a full participant this week but remains on injured reserve. It adds another question mark to the team's backfield situation ahead of Monday's game against the Bengals, and Saturday's injury report will reveal the odds of both players to suit up in the coming days.

items.headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) nearing return from IR
items.news: Croskey-Merritt (groin) said Friday he's taking things "day by day," but his goal is to play Monday against the Bengals, John Keim of ESPN.com reports.
items.analysis: Croskey-Merritt remains on injured reserve, meaning he'll need to be activated by Monday afternoon to have a chance to return in Week 11. Considering he logged full practices Thursday and Friday, he's on track to do so, and if he's able to suit up, he'll rejoin a backfield currently composed of Rachaad White (heel, limited Friday) and Austin Ekeler.

items.headline: Will Shipley (foot/illness) nearing return from IR
items.news: Shipley (foot/illness) didn't practice Friday and is listed as questionable for Sunday's contest versus the Steelers.
items.analysis: Since the Eagles designated Shipley to return from injured reserve Monday, he managed back-to-back limited practices to begin Week 11 prep before Friday's absence, which seemingly can be attributed to an illness. The team will need to activate Shipley from IR by Saturday afternoon for him to have a chance to play Sunday. If he gets the all clear, Shipley will be joining a backfield that's still led by Saquon Barkley, with Jaydon Blue and potentially practice-squad member Elijah Mitchell also available.

items.headline: Darren Waller (knee) listed as questionable
items.news: Waller (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Ravens, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
items.analysis: According to Person, Waller told coach Dave Canales he's ready to play Sunday against Baltimore, so fantasy players should proceed as if Waller will be active. Waller's production has been all over the place this season, making him difficult to pin down as a reliable weekly fantasy option. He's more of a best-ball type of fantasy asset.

items.headline: Brock Bowers (ankle) listed as questionable
items.news: Coach Klint Kubiak said Friday that Bowers (ankle) is slated to be listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Broncos, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
items.analysis: Bowers, who was limited at Thursday's practice, was back on the field Friday, but the tight end nonetheless will head into the weekend with a questionable designation. Look for added intel regarding his Week 11 status to arrive late Saturday or early Sunday via the usual assortment of NFL insiders, but if Bowers is limited or ends up out for his team's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff, fellow TE Michael Mayer will merit fantasy lineup consideration while facing 7-2 Denver.

items.headline: Jordan James (calf) listed as questionable
items.news: James (calf) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Vikings in Mexico City.
items.analysis: James' practice reps were limited both Thursday and Friday due to a calf injury. He was limited to kickoff return duties against the Cowboys in Week 10, and that role could be taken over by Deebo Samuel and/or Jacob Cowing if James is unable to play Sunday.

items.headline: Ihmir Smith-Marsette practice update
items.news: The Panthers cut Smith-Marsette (undisclosed) from the practice squad injured list Friday with an injury settlement, Anthony Rizzuti of USA Today reports.
items.analysis: Smith-Marsette landed on the practice squad injured list Nov. 10 due to an undisclosed injury. Now that he's been let go with an injury settlement, Smith-Marsette will have the opportunity to sign with a team once he's fully healthy. He has not played in a regular-season game since 2024, when he appeared in six contests as a member of the Giants.

items.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) injury update
items.news: Smith (hamstring) practiced fully Thursday.
items.analysis: Smith followed up Wednesday's limited showing with an uncapped session one day later, thereby paving the way for his first game action since Week 6. Despite missing five of the last six contests due to a hamstring injury, he put together a 26-310-2 line on 41 targets in his four appearances this season. However, with Jalen Hurts (blood clots) out for the rest of the 2026 campaign, Smith will be on the receiving end of passes from Joe Milton on Sunday against the Steelers.

items.headline: Caleb Lohner (foot) remains on IR
items.news: Lohner (foot) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.
items.analysis: The Broncos opened Lohner's 21-day practice window Wednesday. The tight end is not quite ready to make his season debut, as he is still tending to his recovery from a foot injury he sustained in the offseason. Lohner was a full participant in all three Week 11 prep sessions, meaning his odds of returning in Week 12 are quite good if he can continue to log full sessions.

items.headline: Britain Covey (knee) injury update
items.news: Covey (knee) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Steelers.
items.analysis: Covey was a limited participant in all three practices during Week 11 prep, but the veteran wide receiver has done enough to be cleared to return from a two-game absence due to a knee injury. He'll likely operate as the Eagles' top return option on kickoffs and punts while providing depth at wide receiver.

items.headline: Brenen Thompson (hamstring) listed as doubtful
items.news: Thompson (hamstring) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Jets.
items.analysis: Thompson has been sidelined by a hamstring injury and has not seen regular-season action since Week 2 against the Raiders. If he's ruled out for Sunday's game, then the rookie fourth-rounder's next chance to play would be Week 12 against the Patriots on Sunday, Nov. 29.

items.headline: Carson Beck (back) listed as questionable
items.news: Beck (back) will not practice Friday, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.analysis: After being listed as limited Thursday, Beck's looming absence from Friday's practice -- the result of back spasms flaring up -- per Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site, clouds his status for Sunday's game at Kansas City. For now, coach Mike LaFleur said the team will proceed as if Josh Johnson will make the start at quarterback, though the door hasn't been completely closed on the possibility of Beck being available. It's a situation to avoid in most fantasy formats.

items.headline: Jared Wayne (quadriceps) ruled out
items.news: Wayne (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Bills, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
items.analysis: Wayne will miss a second straight game due to a quadriceps injury, and his next chance to suit up is Week 12 against the Jets on Sunday, Nov. 29. In his absence, Kevin Coleman and Jalen Tolbert will serve as the Dolphins' rotational wide receivers behind Malik Washington, Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell.

items.headline: Jordyn Tyson (chest) injury update
items.news: Tyson (chest) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game at Chicago.
items.analysis: Tyson opened Week 11 prep with back-to-back limited sessions due to a chest injury, but his return to a full practice Friday has him in the clear for Sunday's matchup. He'll look to build upon the 11-80-0 line on 13 targets the he compiled against the Panthers in Week 10.

items.headline: Tommy Tremble (knee) listed as questionable
items.news: Tremble (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
items.analysis: Tremble put together a DNP-LP-LP practice log during Week 11 prep while managing a knee injury that he picked up during the Panthers' 20-17 win over the Saints in Week 10. Darren Waller (knee) also is listed as questionable, which leaves Mitchell Evans, Feleipe Franks and Ja'Tavion Sanders as the Panthers' healthy tight ends on the 53-man roster heading into the weekend. Tremble's status for Sunday's game may not officially be known until 90 minutes before the 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff, when Carolina announces its list of inactive players.

items.headline: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) injury update
items.news: Meyers (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Giants.
items.analysis: Meyers has been playing through the ankle injury for weeks, so his status was never in real doubt despite limited practices all week. The veteran wideout doesn't have a touchdown catch since Week 3 and has topped 65 receiving yards in a game just once all season. He's a low-floor, low-ceiling fantasy option.

items.headline: Davante Adams (hamstring) remains on IR
items.news: Coach Sean McVay noted Friday that Adams (hamstring) isn't expected to practice this weekend, Greg Beacham of the Associated Press reports.
items.analysis: Regarding the looming practice status of Adams, who is on IR and last played in Week 6, McVay said Friday, "We're not quite there yet." On the plus side, Beacham relays that the Rams still are hopeful Adams will be ready retake the field next week. The veteran pass-catcher's availability gains added import going forward, following Friday's report from Beacham that fellow starting WR Puka Nacua is on track to miss a couple of months after undergoing an MCL procedure.

items.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) injury update
items.news: Barkley (hamstring) told EJ Smith of PHLY Sports on Friday that he "feels better physically" after the team's Week 10 bye, and the running back doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest against the Steelers.
items.analysis: Barkley was able to put together a full week of drills during Week 11 prep, and while his current state is positive, he added that the time off isn't a "magic pill," indicating that he still has some residual effects from the hamstring injury that has lingered since he picked it up in Week 4. In his last appearance in Week 9 against the Giants, he handled a 58 percent snap share and turned his 13 carries into 22 yards and one touchdown. As for the rest of the Eagles backfield, Jaydon Blue is the only other option on the active roster, Elijah Mitchell is a candidate to be elevated from the practice squad, and Will Shipley (foot) may be activated from injured reserve Saturday.

items.headline: Charlie Kolar (concussion) listed as questionable
items.news: Kolar (concussion) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Jets.
items.analysis: The tight end is still in the concussion protocol, so he'll be up against it to clear the final hurdles, especially after the Chargers played Monday night against Baltimore. If Kolar is ruled out, David Njoku and Oronde Gadsden should handle most of the tight-end duties for the Bolts.

items.headline: Ladd McConkey (back) listed as questionable
items.news: McConkey (back) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Jets.
items.analysis: McConkey, who didn't record any snaps during Week 9 action due to back spasms and was inactive in Week 10, has been able to practice in a limited fashion thus far this week, but thanks to his official 'questionable' designation, his status will need to be tracked in advance of Sunday's 4:05 ET kickoff. If McConkey is limited or out versus New York, Tre' Harris could maintain a key role in the Chargers' pass-catching corps alongside fellow WR Quentin Johnston.

items.headline: Isaiah Likely (undisclosed) practice update
items.news: Likely (undisclosed) wasn't spotted at Friday's practice, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.
items.analysis: That said, Duggan noted that he did see Likely, who hasn't been on the Giants' Week 11 injury report so far, walking into the building after the team's Friday morning walkthrough. In any case, New York's upcoming practice report will provide context regarding Likely's apparent absence, as well as his official status for Sunday's game against the Jaguars.

items.headline: Luke Schoonmaker (illness) listed as questionable
items.news: Schoonmaker (illness) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Titans, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
items.analysis: Schoonmaker was held out of practice Thursday and Friday due to an illness, and he's drawn the questionable tag heading into the weekend. Jake Ferguson (knee) has already been ruled out, and with Schoonmaker under the weather, that leaves Brevyn Spann-Ford and James Mitchell as the Cowboys' two healthy tight ends on the 53-man roster ahead of Sunday's contest. Michael Trigg could be elevated from the practice squad to the active roster depending on Schoonmaker's recovery.

items.headline: Jonathan Mingo (ankle/foot) ruled out
items.news: Mingo (ankle/foot) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Titans, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
items.analysis: It will be the second game that Mingo will miss while recovering from foot and ankle injuries, which have prevented him from practicing over the last two weeks, and his next chance to suit up is Week 12 against the Eagles on Thanksgiving Day. In Mingo's absence, KaVontae Turpin and Camden Brown will be the Cowboys' rotational options at wide receiver behind CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and Ryan Flournoy.

items.headline: Jeshaun Jones (shoulder) injury update
items.news: Jones (shoulder) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the 49ers in Mexico City.
items.analysis: Jones -- who was managing a shoulder injury during Week 11 prep -- was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. He was signed to the Vikings' 53-man roster Wednesday to give the team more depth at wide receiver while Jordan Addison recovers from a thumb injury. Jones figures to be limited to a rotational role on offense while serving as a contributor on special teams.

items.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle/foot) ruled out
items.news: Wicks (ankle/foot) is listed as out for Sunday's game against the Steelers.
items.analysis: Wicks had been trending toward a possible return after practicing in a limited fashion throughout the week, but he'll remain unavailable for at least one more game, and it's worth pointing out that the foot designation is a new one for the wide receiver. It's possible he was injured in practice Friday. The Eagles have a quick turnaround for Week 12 against the Cowboys on Thanksgiving, so perhaps Wicks will be available for that contest.

items.headline: Jaylen Waddle (concussion) practice update
items.news: Waddle (concussion) doesn't carry an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Raiders after practicing fully this week.
items.analysis: Waddle was limited to just 14 snaps and one catch for 22 yards before exiting the Broncos' Week 9 win over the Panthers with a concussion. Following a well-time Week 10 bye, Waddle has progressed through the NFL's concussion protocol, ensuring that Denver's top pass catcher -- who has recorded a 30/337/2 receiving line on 52 targets through nine contests -- will be available this weekend.

items.headline: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) practice update
items.news: Tuten (ankle/foot) was present for the stretching portion of Friday's practice before moving to a side field, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
items.analysis: Tuten was deemed limited at practice Wednesday and then was a non-participant Thursday. It remains to be seen how the Jaguars classify his participation (or lack thereof) in Friday's session, with added clarity on that front set to arrive via the team's upcoming injury report.

items.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) listed as questionable
items.news: Tate (shoulder), who was a full participant in Friday's practice, is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Cowboys.
items.analysis: After logging limited practices both Wednesday and Thursday, Tate upgraded to full participation to close the week, which has him trending in the right direction ahead of Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff. Earlier Friday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site relayed that coach Robert Saleh said Tate had a really good week, noting that the WR had a moment during Thursday's session when he made a diving catch, landed on his shoulder and was able to get up without any problem.

items.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) listed as questionable
items.news: Spears (knee) is questionable for Sunday's game against Dallas.
items.analysis: The running back practiced fully Friday, so he should be good to go for Sunday's contest after he returned from a two-game absence last week against the Jaguars to play 16 snaps behind Tony Pollard. Spears is a desperation fantasy play in a week with six teams on bye.

items.headline: Jordan Addison (thumb) listed as out
items.news: Head coach Kevin O'Connell said Wednesday that Addison underwent thumb surgery earlier this week and won't be placed on injured reserve, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports.
items.analysis: Thus, the Vikings are expecting Addison to recover fully before the four games required of an IR stint, but in any case he will miss some time due to the thumb injury he suffered in practice last Friday and sidelined him this past Sunday at Green Bay. With Addison out of the lineup, Minnesota will be relying on Justin Jefferson, Jauan Jennings (calf), Myles Price, Tai Felton and Jeshaun Jones at wide receiver.

items.headline: Joe Burrow (illness) injury update
items.news: Burrow (illness) said Friday that he's getting better, noting that he "for sure" feels optimistic he'll be at full strength for Monday night's game against the Commanders, Kelsey Conway of The Cincinnati Enquirer reports.
items.analysis: Burrow is managing what the Bengals list as an illness, but the QB was a full participant in Thursday's practice and is trending toward approaching Monday night's game without a Week 11 designation. Official confirmation of that expected outcome will arrive Saturday, either way.

items.headline: Jauan Jennings (calf) injury update
items.news: Jennings (calf) practiced in full Wednesday.
items.analysis: Jennings sat out the last two games due to a calf injury, but his return to all activity Wednesday gives the Vikings' receiving corps a boost after Jordan Addison was lost for at least a few weeks due to a broken thumb that required surgery. As for Jennings, he'll have a prime opportunity to work opposite No. 1 WR Justin Jefferson as he looks to build upon his 6-54-0 line on 10 targets in his six appearances this season.

items.headline: T.J. Hockenson (wrist) injury update
items.news: Hockenson (wrist) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday night's game against the 49ers.
items.analysis: After sitting out last Sunday against Green Bay and then logging limited practices Wednesday and Thursday, Hockenson is ready to return against San Francisco in a potential playoff preview. His lack of a designation puts Minnesota's top tight end in position to reclaim his usual role in the passing game that now has Kirk Cousins at quarterback. Hockenson is a TE1 for fantasy purposes.

items.headline: Jake Ferguson (knee) listed as out
items.news: Ferguson didn't practice Wednesday due to knee and ankle injuries and won't be available for Sunday's game against the Titans, Todd Archer of ESPN.com reports.
items.analysis: Ferguson injured his knee in a Week 9 win over the Colts, while the ankle issue is more of a lingering concern after he initially sustained a low sprain in a Week 8 loss to the Cardinals. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer previously announced Nov. 9 that Ferguson was set to miss multiple weeks, so the tight end's continued absence from practice comes as little surprise. In Ferguson's stead, Brevyn Spann-Ford should be in line for another turn as Dallas' top tight end in Week 11.

items.headline: Travis Kelce (ankle/calf) injury update
items.news: Kelce (ankle/calf) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
items.analysis: Kelce was forced from last Sunday's game against the Falcons with the ankle injury, but he's good to go for Week 11 against a hapless Arizona squad. The Chiefs should run all over the Cardinals defense and likely won't need much pass volume from Patrick Mahomes. Kelce is more of a fringe TE1 for fantasy purposes.

items.headline: Zavion Thomas (ankle) listed as questionable
items.news: Thomas (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's matchup against the Saints.
items.analysis: Thomas appears to have picked up an injury in the Bears' lead-up to Week 11, as he did not participate in Friday's practice. The rookie third-rounder acts as the team's top kick-return option. Should he not play, Josh Blackwell may take over duties on special teams.

items.headline: Ray Davis (hamstring) injury update
items.news: Davis (hamstring) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
items.analysis: The backup running back was managed during the practice week but is good to go for his normal role behind lead back James Cook. With the Bills listed as 16.5-point favorites, Davis could see some extra reps in garbage time if Buffalo does indeed blow out Miami.

items.headline: Emeka Egbuka (foot) injury update
items.news: Egbuka (foot) caught three of five targets for 38 yards and added a one-yard run in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
items.analysis: Egbuka returned from a two-game absence during which he was in concussion protocol in addition to dealing with a foot injury. He tied for second on the team in targets behind Cade Otton's eight and finished third in receiving yards behind Tez Johnson (76) and Kenny Gainwell (60), as Baker Mayfield spread the ball around to complement Bucky Irving's two-touchdown effort on the ground. Egbuka hasn't exceeded 63 yards in seven appearances this season heading into Tampa Bay's Week 10 bye.

items.headline: Kenneth Walker III (groin) ruled out
items.news: Walker (groin) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
items.analysis: Walker, who wasn't able to practice this week, will thus target a potential return Thursday against the Bills. The Chiefs -- per ESPN.com -- are "optimistic" he will play Thanksgiving night, but they will err on the side of caution with a short week ahead, and as such Emmett Johnson -- who rushed 22 times for 101 yards and brought in six of seven targets for 70 yards and two touchdowns in Week 10 -- is headed toward a second consecutive start this weekend.

items.headline: A.J. Brown (hamstring) listed as doubtful
items.news: Brown (hamstring) is expected to miss multiple weeks, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
items.analysis: New England's trade for Brown is going down as one the team would definitely prefer to reverse. He's shown no chemistry with Drake Maye (ankle) and hasn't looked healthy since injuring his ankle in the first half of the Week 1 game against the Seahawks. Brown also appears to have lost multiple steps with his downfield speed due to the laundry list of lower-body injuries that now includes ankle, knee and hamstring issues in 2026. The Patriots will play out the string on a lost season without Maye and Brown for several more weeks. Look for Mack Hollins, Romeo Doubs (shoulder, IR) when healthy, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism to pick up the slack at wideout with Brown on the shelf again.

items.headline: Drake Maye (ankle) listed as out
items.news: Maye has suffered a fractured right fibula that won't require surgery but is expected to sideline him for some time, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
items.analysis: Maye was knocked out of Week 10 action on the first possession of this past Sunday's loss to the Lions in Munich. He already was expected to miss multiple games as a result of the injury, but with a diagnosis now available, he's now in rehab mode until further notice. A return at some point down the stretch likely will depend on the Patriots remaining in the playoff race, but for the time being Tommy DeVito will be under center in place of Maye.

items.headline: Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) listed as doubtful
items.news: Kincaid (thumb/ankle) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Dolphins, Matt Parrino reports.
items.analysis: The Bills are massive 16.5-point favorites at home against a Dolphins team missing its starting quarterback, so it presents an opportunity to give Kincaid a rest after he's been playing through injuries the last several weeks. Dawson Knox will remain an every-down tight end, with Jackson Hawes and Keleki Latu stepping into elevated spots. The biggest beneficiaries likely will be DJ Moore and Khalil Shakir in terms of target opportunities, though Buffalo should run all over this Miami defense.

items.headline: Terrance Ferguson (hamstring/ankle) placed on IR
items.news: Ferguson (hamstring/ankle) isn't ready to return to game action, but the Rams still plan to activate him from injured reserve before Week 12 and keep him on the active roster, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
items.analysis: Even if Ferguson is moved back to the active roster, coach Sean McVay's comments indicate the tight end still won't be ready to play coming out of the team's Week 11 bye. His activation at least would keep him off season-ending IR, but his near-term availability remains uncertain until the Rams signal he's ready for game action. With Puka Nacua (knee/toe) likely done for the remainder of the regular season following MCL surgery, Ferguson and Davante Adams (hamstring) are needed badly in this offense.

items.headline: Kayshon Boutte (hip) listed as questionable
items.news: Boutte's hip injury he suffered in Thursday night's win over the Colts doesn't appear to be serious, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
items.analysis: The wideout had one of his more productive games of the season before being injured, as he caught both of his targets for 40 yards and a touchdown. His 40 yards were the second-most he's produced in a game this season. Boutte is up to 21 grabs for 359 yards and three touchdowns on 31 targets across 10 games in 2026.

items.headline: Isaiah Williams (ribs) ruled out
items.news: Williams (ribs) won't play in Sunday's game against the Chargers.
items.analysis: With Omar Cooper (ankle/hip) also slated to be unavailable for the contest, Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell will lead the Jets' Week 11 WR corps, with coach Aaron Glenn noting Friday that the team's tight ends, primarily Kenyon Sadiq and Mason Taylor, should have an opportunity to see added opportunities as pass catchers this weekend in the absence of both Cooper and Williams.

items.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) ruled out
items.news: Coach Aaron Glenn said Friday that Cooper (ankle/hip) will be out for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
items.analysis: Cooper didn't practice Wednesday or Thursday due to a pair of injuries, and he'll wind up sitting out Week 11. Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell will be the primary wideouts for the Jets, and with Isaiah Williams (ribs) joining Cooper on the sidelines, Malik McClain and Tim Patrick will be options when the team wants to get more receivers on the field, and per head coach Aaron Glenn -- via Rich Cimini of ESPN.com -- Sterling Shepard and tight ends Kenyon Sadiq and Mason Taylor could also get involved.

items.headline: Seth McGowan (hamstring) listed as questionable
items.news: McGowan (hamstring) has been ruled out for the rest of Thursday's game against the Texans, Jane Slater of NFL Network reports.
items.analysis: McGowan was injured just before halftime while returning a kickoff. He was deemed questionable to return at the beginning of the third quarter and subsequently was ruled out shortly thereafter. The rookie running back gained seven yards on three carries and caught his only target for one yard before exiting while adding 117 yards on three kickoff returns. Jonathan Taylor should continue to get most of the work at running back for the Colts for the rest of the game, and DJ Giddens should handle whatever backfield snaps that Taylor doesn't get.

items.headline: Mac Jones (illness) practice update
items.news: Jones (illness) did not participate at practice Thursday.
items.analysis: Jones popped up on the 49ers' injury report with an unspecified illness Wednesday, and now his status for Week 11 is up in the air. If he can't practice in full Friday, there's a decent chance he'll end up carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

items.headline: Colson Yankoff (knee) practice update
items.news: Yankoff (knee) was a full participant at practice Thursday.
items.analysis: Yankoff sat out the Commanders' contest against the Giants in Week 10 because of a knee injury, but it now looks like he's put it behind him. He figures to resume a depth role at tight end in Week 11 against the Bengals.

items.headline: Isaac Guerendo (pectoral) listed as out
items.news: Guerendo (pectoral) was working off to the side during practice Thursday, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
items.analysis: Guerendo has been on the PUP list with a pec injury since training camp, but it now looks like he may be making some progress toward returning to action. Even if he does get back to full strength at some point soon, though, it's not clear how much room there will be for him in a 49ers' backfield that has recently been dominated by veteran Christian McCaffrey and rookie third-rounder Kaelon Black.

items.headline: Andrei Iosivas (thumb) remains on IR
items.news: Iosivas (thumb) practiced fully Thursday, Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic reports.
items.analysis: Iosivas had his 21-day practice window opened last week but remains on injured reserve. With Dohnte Meyers playing well as the Bengals' WR3, there's likely no rush to activate Iosivas, who has just 87 career regular-season catches across 52 appearances. He's averaged 20.2 receiving yards per game in his career.

items.headline: Tee Higgins (knee) practice update
items.news: Higgins (knee) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic reports.
items.analysis: It's a new "injury" for Higgins, but the full participation level suggests it's nothing serious after the wideout was managed late in last Sunday night's blowout win over the Steelers, per Kelsey Conway of The Cincinnati Enquirer. Higgins already has a fantasy-friendly 53 catches (on 73 targets) for 824 yards and six touchdowns through nine games. He's on pace for a career year in 2026.

items.headline: Lamar Jackson (thumb) remains on IR
items.news: The Ravens believe "there's a chance" that Jackson (thumb) could return for their Week 16 matchup with the Browns, assuming all goes well in his recovery from right thumb surgery, Dan Graziano of ESPN.com reports.
items.analysis: Last Friday, head coach Jesse Minter announced that Jackson was facing a projected recovery timeline of 6-to-10 weeks after requiring a procedure to address a broken and dislocated thumb. A Week 16 return would be right up against the short end of that timeline, so if Jackson has shown notable improvement by that point, he could push to play if the 4-6 Ravens haven't faded from the playoff picture. While Jackson remains sidelined for at least a few more weeks, the Ravens will entrust trade-deadline acquisition Jacoby Brissett to direct the offense.

items.headline: Christian Kirk (meniscus) remains on IR
items.news: Kirk announced Wednesday via his personal Instagram account that he recently underwent meniscus surgery.
items.analysis: After he had missed the 49ers' first six games of the season while recovering from a calf injury, Kirk landed on injured reserve for the second time this season back on Nov. 7 due to a right knee injury sustained in his team debut Week 7 in Atlanta. Since Kirk didn't specify whether he required a partial meniscectomy or a meniscus repair, his exact recovery timeline isn't known. Regardless, he'll have to miss at least two more games while he's on IR.

items.headline: Jackson Hawes (shoulder) injury update
items.news: Hawes (shoulder) was a late addition to Wednesday's injury report, Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News.
items.analysis: It is unclear whether Hawes suffered his shoulder injury, however, his eligibility for Week 11 against the Dolphins will likely be decided during the Thursday and Friday prep sessions. The 25-year-old will need to upgrade to a full participant by Friday's practice to avoid any injury designation ahead of Sunday's contest.

items.headline: Jared Wiley (ankle) placed on IR
items.news: The Chiefs placed Wiley (ankle) on injured reserve Wednesday, Matt Derrick of ChiefsDigest.com reports.
items.analysis: Wiley was carted to the locker room in the first quarter of the Chiefs' Week 10 win over the Falcons with an ankle injury. The tight end will now be on IR as he nurses his fractured ankle until at least the latter part of the regular season. Travis Kelce, Noah Gray and Jake Briningstool are now the only tight ends on the Chiefs' active roster.

items.headline: CJ Donaldson (shoulder) practice update
items.news: Donaldson (shoulder) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
items.analysis: Donaldson missed the Saints' last three games due to a shoulder injury, but his full practice Wednesday indicates that he'll be available for Sunday's road game against the Bears. Even if Donaldson does suit up, his role in the backfield figures to be minimal, seeing as Travis Etienne is off injured reserve and Alvin Kamara and Audric Estime are also available for the Saints.

items.headline: Jaydn Ott (hamstring) practice update
items.news: Ott (hamstring) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
items.analysis: Ott was unable to play against the Falcons in Week 10 due to a hamstring injury. However, the undrafted rookie out of Oklahoma was cleared to practice in full Wednesday, so he should be available for Sunday's home game against the Cardinals. If Kenneth Walker (groin) cannot play in Week 11, then Ott would have the opportunity to serve as the Chiefs' RB2 behind rookie fifth-rounder Emmett Johnson.

items.headline: Brevin Jordan (foot) ruled out
items.news: Jordan (foot/illness) has been ruled out ahead of Thursday night's game against the Colts.
items.analysis: Jordan missed all three Week 11 practice sessions due to an injury and an illness. The tight end will miss a second straight game, this time with two separate issues as opposed to the finger injury that plagued him ahead of Week 10. Marlin Klein or Cade Stover is set to be the No. 3 tight end behind Dalton Schultz and Foster Moreau for Thursday night's contest.

items.headline: De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) remains on IR
items.news: Stribling (ankle) was doing some work on the side at Wednesday's practice, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
items.analysis: This is the first time Stribling has participated in on-field work since suffering a significant ankle injury in the Week 1 win over the Rams. The expectation has been that the rookie could be back by December, so Stribling is progressing toward hitting that goal. Once Stribling progresses to full-team drills, his timeline will get more dialed in. The 49ers have two more games in November, leaving the Week 13 matchup against the Giants as his earliest potential return date.

items.headline: James Conner (foot) placed on IR
items.news: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Wednesday that he has no new updates on the status of Conner (foot), who is still "working to return to perform," Tyler Drake of ArizonaSports.com reports. "It was not a good injury," LaFleur said.
items.analysis: Conner hasn't played in a game since Week 3 of last season, when he sustained a right foot/ankle injury that required surgery. Though he was able to participate in individual drills in training camp, he never advanced to team work before being placed on injured reserve with a designation to return Aug. 30. The Cardinals still haven't cleared Conner to practice nearly three months later, which suggests that he either experienced a setback over the summer or plateaued in his recovery. Whatever the case, Conner doesn't seem close to a return, and the chances of him playing at any point this season will grow dimmer with each week that he doesn't practice.

items.headline: Will Mallory (hamstring) ruled out
items.news: The Colts ruled out Mallory (hamstring) for Thursday night's games against the Texans.
items.analysis: Mallory was absent from practice all week heading into Thursday night's divisional showdown versus Houston. This marks the 27-year-old's third straight missed game. He has caught two of nine targets for 20 yards in three games during the 2026 season.

items.headline: Tyrone Tracy Jr. (hamstring) remains on IR
items.news: Tracy (hamstring) could be reinstated from injured reserve when first eligible ahead of the Giants' Week 13 game against the 49ers, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.
items.analysis: The Giants haven't provided any updates on Tracy since he landed on IR on Oct. 27 after sustaining a hamstring strain in a Week 7 win over the Texans, but the running back is seemingly progressing well and could be ready to play once he sits out the required four games. Once he's reinstated, Tracy could operate as a change-of-pace option behind Cam Skattebo, who appears to have reclaimed the lead role out of the New York backfield after a one-game benching in Week 6.

items.headline: Brandon Aiyuk (ACL + MCL) ruled out
items.news: Aiyuk's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said Tuesday that the receiver is "100 percent healthy" and fully recovered from his November 2024 right knee surgery and plans to work out for interested teams once he's released by the 49ers, Dianna Russini of BetUS TV reports.
items.analysis: After Aiyuk filed his paperwork for reinstatement, San Francisco activated him from the reserve/left squad list Nov. 9. Rosenhaus noted that Aiyuk passed his physical at that time, with MRIs and X-rays on his surgically repaired knee revealing no concerns. The 49ers were granted a two-week roster exemption for Aiyuk that will expire next Monday, and the 28-year-old wideout is expected to be cut loose at that time since San Francisco seemingly hasn't expressed interested in retaining him. While it's unclear what kind of market might exist for Aiyuk's services coming off a lengthy layoff from NFL action, NFL reporter Jordan Schultz relayed earlier this month that at least one NFC team has expressed interest in adding the receiver to its practice squad.

items.headline: Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) placed on IR
items.news: Coach Robert Saleh said Wednesday that Robinson (ankle) -- who was placed on IR on Tuesady -- is out for the rest of the season, Terry McCormick of TitanInsider.com reports.
items.analysis: Meanwhile Carnell Tate (shoulder) is slated to practice this week, and his potential return to action this weekend against Dallas figures to impact the playing time of Elic Ayomanor and Chimere Dike. Robinson's looming absence will free up snaps/targets in the slot, with Saleh noting Wednesday that he's looking forward to seeing what rookie slot option Xavier Restrepo can do with added opportunities going forward.

items.headline: Gardner Minshew II (elbow) remains on IR
items.news: Minshew (elbow) underwent UCL reconstructive surgery Monday, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
items.analysis: Though the procedure will bring an end to Minshew's season, he's expected to make a full recovery ahead of the 2027 campaign. The veteran quarterback sustained the injury while making his lone start of the season Week 9 in Seattle, but he played though the elbow issue and completed 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards. Rookie third-round pick Carson Beck took over as the Cardinals' starting quarterback in Week 10 and is expected to lead the offense for the remainder of the season.

items.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) remains on IR
items.news: Henderson is on injured reserve with an illness injury.

items.headline: Sam Darnold (quadriceps/ribs) listed as out
items.news: Head coach Mike Macdonald said Monday that he's "really optimistic" Darnold (quadriceps/ribs) will be able to get a full week's worth of practice coming out of the Seahawks' Week 11 bye and start their next game Sunday, Nov. 29, against the 49ers, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.
items.analysis: Darnold, who last played in Week 8, still is working his way through a pair of injuries, but barring any setbacks, he's trending toward a Week 12 return. Macdonald reiterated that Darnold will be the team's starter once healthy, even though backup Drew Lock has guided Seattle to a 4-0 record while coming on in relief or starting in place of an injured Darnold in the first two games of the season as well as the most recent two contests.

items.headline: Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) practice update
items.news: Harrison (hamstring) was a non-participant in Tuesday's practice.
items.analysis: While the Texans haven't provided a definitive word on Harrison's status for Thursday's game against the Colts, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston relays that the 24-year-old wideout is trending toward missing a second straight contest now that he's yet to practice in any fashion this week. Since being acquired from the Cardinals in October, Harrison has suited up in three games for Houston and has recorded six catches for 60 yards and a touchdown on 11 targets.

items.headline: Woody Marks (concussion) ruled out
items.news: Marks (concussion) didn't practice Tuesday.
items.analysis: Marks' continued absence at practice comes as little surprise after he entered concussion protocol upon sustaining a head injury in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Browns. Head coach DeMeco Ryans has already indicated that Marks is unlikely to clear the five-step protocol ahead of Thursday's game against the Colts, so expect the second-year back to get formally ruled out for the Week 11 contest following Wednesday's practice.

items.headline: Josh Jacobs (finger) listed as out
items.news: Jacobs (finger) has a "realistic chance" of returning to action Nov. 25 against the Rams following the Packers' Week 11 bye, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
items.analysis: Jacobs sustained a fractured right ring finger in the Packers' Nov. 8 win over the Patriots and underwent surgery this past Friday, with the procedure carrying a projected recovery timeline of 2-to-3 weeks. The veteran running back sat out Sunday's 30-10 win over the Vikings, but that could end up being the extent of his absence, as a well-timed Week 11 bye gives him a shot at returning at the short end of his estimated recovery timetable. Kaleb Johnson stepped up as Green Bay's top option out of the backfield while Jacobs has been sidelined for most of the past two games, carrying 24 times for 110 yards and a touchdown between those contests.

items.headline: Tyler Loop (groin) remains on IR
items.news: Loop is on injured reserve with a groin injury.

items.headline: Skyy Moore (ankle) listed as questionable
items.news: Moore's ankle injury is not considered serious, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
items.analysis: The Packers' decision to rule Moore out with an ankle injury in the Week 10 loss to the Vikings was a precautionary move after the 26-year-old made his first appearance since returning from injured reserve. It's unclear if the fifth-year pro will be sidelined for any coming games, but Savion Williams and Matthew Golden will likely act as primary return options if Moore misses any time.

items.headline: Adam Randall (neck/hamstring) nearing return from IR
items.news: Randall (neck/hamstring) wasn't activated from injured reserve and will remain out for Monday's game against the Chargers, Brian Wacker of The Baltimore Sun reports.
items.analysis: A rookie fifth-round pick out of Clemson, Randall is still waiting to make his NFL debut while he's spent all season on IR due to a neck injury. He had his 21-day evaluation window opened Oct. 28 and has been a full participant in practices each of the last three weeks, but the Ravens haven't elected to reinstate him. His window will come to a close Wednesday, so if he's not activated by then, the 22-year-old running back will remain on IR for the rest of the season.

items.headline: George Holani (knee) listed as questionable
items.news: Holani is week-to-week after suffering an MCL sprain in Sunday's win over Las Vegas, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Monday.
items.analysis: Holani exited Sunday's Week 10 game against the Raiders after suffering a knee injury. The 26-year-old is not currently expected to be placed on injured reserve, but he will be reevaluated after Seattle's Week 11 bye. The three-year pro has had a larger role on special teams since Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price returned from injuries to helm Seattle's ground attack.

items.headline: Drake London (head) injury update
items.news: Head coach Kevin Stefanski said Monday that London was cleared of a concussion near the end of Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Chiefs, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
items.analysis: London was checked for a possible concussion in the fourth quarter of Week 10 action, but the result of the evaluation wasn't reported before the game concluded. Prior to his exit Sunday, he posted his third 100-yard game (109, to be exact) of the campaign on six catches and a season-high 12 targets. London will continue to operate as the Falcons' No. 1 WR after a Week 11 bye in the team's next game Sunday, Nov. 29, at Minnesota.

items.headline: Malik Willis (groin/core) remains on IR
items.news: Head coach Jeff Hafley said Monday that Willis (groin/core) has not undergone surgery and that the Dolphins are still determining if a procedure is needed, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
items.analysis: Per Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald, Hafley noted on that subject Monday, "We will see how he feels. If he needs surgery, he will have surgery," while adding that if the QB does undergo a procedure, it wouldn't "necessarily" be season ending. In any case, the earliest Willis can come off IR is Week 14, with Kyle McCord and Brady Cook currently available to handle Miami's signal-caller duties.

items.headline: RJ Harvey (knee) remains on IR
items.news: Harvey is on injured reserve with a knee injury.

items.headline: Bo Melton (thigh) listed as questionable
items.news: Melton (thigh) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Vikings, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
items.analysis: Melton exited Sunday's game because of a thigh injury, and he will not be cleared to return to the contest. Skyy Moore (ankle) will also not return, so Savion Williams and Matthew Golden will operate as the top return options on kickoffs and punts.

items.headline: Mo Alie-Cox (groin) remains on IR
items.news: Alie-Cox is on injured reserve with a groin injury.

items.headline: Josh Whyle (concussion) placed on IR
items.news: Green Bay placed Whyle (concussion) on injured reserve Saturday.
items.analysis: Whyle suffered a concussion in Week 8 against Carolina and missed last Sunday's win over the Patriots. He had already been ruled for Sunday's contest against Minnesota before the Packers decided to place him on IR. Whyle didn't log a catch or target during his eight contests before getting hurt, so his blocking and work on special teams will be the primary voids during his absence.

items.headline: Tyrell Shavers (knee) on PUP list
items.news: The Bills did not activate Shavers (knee) from the reserve/PUP list, and he will not be available for Sunday's game against the Jets.
items.analysis: Shavers drew the questionable tag for Sunday's game against the Jets after logging a trio of full practices during Week 10 prep. However, he was not activated from the PUP list before the 4:00 p.m. ET deadline Saturday, so he will have to wait at least one more week before making his 2026 debut. Shavers' next chance to play is Week 11 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 22.

items.headline: Tyler Goodson (ACL + MCL) placed on IR
items.news: The Cowboys placed Goodson (knee) on injured reserve Saturday, Tommy Yarrish of the team's official site reports.
items.analysis: The move comes as no surprise, seeing as Goodson is expected to miss multiple games due to ACL and MCL sprains in his knee that he suffered during the Cowboys' Week 9 victory over the Colts. With Malik Davis (hip, IR) out for the year and Goodson now on IR, Israel Abanikanda -- who was elevated from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday -- will serve as Dallas' RB2 behind Javonte Williams for Sunday's game against the 49ers. Goodson is required to miss at least four games while on IR, so his next chance to play is Week 15 against the Rams on Sunday, Dec. 20.

items.headline: Chris Collier listed as questionable
items.news: Collier is listed as questionable.

items.headline: Carson Wentz (ankle) injury update
items.news: Wentz (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Green Bay, but Kirk Cousins will be Minnesota's starting quarterback.
items.analysis: Kyler Murray (hamstring) is out for another week but may eventually replace Wentz as the No. 2 quarterback. Wentz's miserable performance against the Bills last week likely was a factor in the Vikings trading for Cousins.

items.news: Branch is listed as out with a hamstring injury.

items.headline: Jalen McMillan (knee) placed on IR
items.news: Head coach Todd Bowles suggested Monday that McMillan (knee) isn't likely to immediately return to action following the Buccaneers' Week 10 bye, Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times reports.
items.analysis: While Bowles indicated that linebacker Yaya Diaby (knee) has decent odds of playing in the Buccaneers' next game Nov. 22 versus the Lions, the coach was less optimistic about McMillan's chances of being ready to play in Week 11. The Buccaneers have yet to open McMillan's 21-day practice window, after he was placed on injured reserve Sept. 30 due to a PCL sprain in his left knee, which was an aggravation of a previous injury. Bowles noted that McMillan underwent a medical procedure on the knee shortly after landing on IR and is still dealing with some discomfort.

items.news: The Bears placed Scott (wrist) on injured reserve Thursday.
items.analysis: Scott will be required to miss at least the next four games. He's appeared in four contests this season, playing 65 snaps on special teams.
